items.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 25 at 4:42AM EDT until September 25 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Up to 1 foot of inundation is
possible for sound-side flooding as strong N'rly winds remain
in place today. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip
currents and large breaking waves expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 11 PM EDT Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT Friday through
Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Portions of Highway 12
will be inundated. Low lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be
inundated. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw
a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck
and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide Friday is 7:02 AM and 7:22 PM.
The most likely time for strong rip currents to occur is a
couple hours either side of low tide, which will occur around
1:15 PM Friday.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued September 25 at 1:46AM EDT until September 26 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...North winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas
15 to 20 ft.

* WHERE...The coastal and offshore waters from Cape Hatteras to
Ocracoke Inlet.

* WHEN...Until 2 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
